hunks.baseline: It was a resonance.
hunks.sol: It was a reverberation.

hunks.baseline: More than a simple roar—a resonance that made their ears ring.
hunks.sol: More than a roar—a sound that left their ears muffled.

hunks.baseline: Darkness and flames collided. At the same time, they swirled together.
hunks.sol: Darkness and flames collided, then mingled.

hunks.baseline: As everyone watched the two incomparably powerful forces suck in wind, air, and debris, slowly swelling, a single word flashed through their minds beneath a red warning light.
hunks.sol: Everyone watched as the two immense forces drew in wind, air, and debris, slowly swelling. A red warning light flashed through their minds, along with a single word.

hunks.baseline: In the face of that immense power, unlike anything they had ever felt, everything seemed meaningless.
hunks.sol: Before power unlike anything they had ever felt, everything else seemed meaningless.

hunks.baseline: If it burst as it was, everything within a few hundred meters would be reduced to ash.
hunks.sol: If it burst, everything within a few hundred meters would turn to ash.

hunks.baseline: No—not just the National Assembly. The fallout might reach the entire city.
hunks.sol: No—the blast might reach beyond the National Assembly and sweep across the entire city.

hunks.baseline: *At this rate…… even the civilians will get hurt.*
hunks.sol: *At this rate… even the civilians will get hurt.*

hunks.baseline: But not everyone thought that way.
hunks.sol: But not everyone was thinking of the civilians.

hunks.baseline: Even if they all felt the same crisis, their circumstances were different.
Some here were fighting to protect the world where everyone outside lived. Others had turned their weapons against them for the sole purpose of protecting their own world.
hunks.sol: They might all have sensed the same danger, but they stood on opposite sides of it. Some fought to protect the world of the people outside. Others had turned their weapons on them to protect only their own.

hunks.baseline: And that one fundamental difference soon showed itself in the actions each side took.
hunks.sol: That difference soon showed in what each side did.

hunks.baseline: With their backs against the cliff, there was nowhere left to retreat.
hunks.sol: With their backs to the cliff’s edge, the traitors had nowhere left to retreat.

hunks.baseline: The traitors who had chosen Michael Silbert seized the chance presented by this sudden turn of events, even as they were already outnumbered, and made one last desperate stand.
hunks.sol: Already outnumbered, those who had chosen Michael Silbert seized on the sudden upheaval and made one last desperate attack.

hunks.baseline: Their numbers had already been cut in half, but the malice in their auras gleamed more viciously than ever.
hunks.sol: Their numbers had been cut in half, but their auras flashed with more vicious intent than ever.

hunks.baseline: A massive tower shield split apart, and the ground cracked like a block of tofu.
hunks.sol: A massive tower shield split apart. The ground opened like a block of tofu under a knife.

hunks.baseline: Strikes came rushing in from every direction, each one lethal if they let their guard down for even a moment. Yet no one stepped back.
hunks.sol: Lethal strikes rushed in from every direction. A moment’s carelessness would cost someone their life, yet no one stepped back.

hunks.baseline: Because they were Hunters.
hunks.sol: They were Hunters.

hunks.baseline: Even if the word meant nothing more to those traitors than a faded slogan, they had upheld what it meant to be a Hunter—and they would continue to do so.
hunks.sol: To the traitors, the word might have been nothing but a faded slogan. The others had lived up to its meaning, and they would keep doing so.

hunks.baseline: It was their duty. The responsibility that came with their strength.
hunks.sol: That was their duty. The responsibility that came with their strength.

hunks.baseline: Choi Minwoo shouted like a battle cry and swung his sword with all his might.
hunks.sol: Choi Minwoo shouted as if giving a battle cry and swung his sword with all his might.

hunks.baseline: Unlike its owner, who was now little more than a man drenched in blood, the dazzling crescent of aura shot across the air, passing close to the towering Black man standing there and cleaving through the dozens of arrows flying toward him.
hunks.sol: Its wielder was drenched in blood, but a dazzling crescent of aura swept through the air, grazed past the towering Black man standing there, and cleaved the dozens of arrows flying toward him.

hunks.baseline: The arrows fell apart in an instant, their severed remains scattering before him.
hunks.sol: The severed arrows scattered before Johnson’s eyes.

hunks.baseline: But even amid the urgent crisis unfolding all around him, Magic Johnson drew a deep breath and gathered his mana, muttering to himself.
hunks.sol: Even amid the battle raging on every side, Magic Johnson drew a deep breath and gathered his mana, muttering to himself.

hunks.baseline: *Just call me Johnson, already.*
hunks.sol: *I keep telling him to call me Johnson.*

hunks.baseline: When this battle was over, when the endless flow of blood had finally stopped, he would tell Choi Minwoo again.
hunks.sol: When this battle was over—when the blood finally stopped flowing—he would tell Choi Minwoo again that there was no need to be so formal with him.

hunks.baseline: He really could speak casually with him now.

He wanted to clap Pai Chen on the shoulder, still drawing his bowstring until his fingers were raw with blood; Prince Felix, fighting drenched in blood despite his noble status; and Chuck Hagel, who had just brutally ripped off the Kronos Guild Master’s arm.
hunks.sol: He wanted to clap Pai Chen on the shoulder as the man drew his bowstring with bloodied fingers. Prince Felix, too, fighting drenched in blood despite his noble station. And Chuck Hagel, who had just ripped off the Kronos Guild Master’s arm.

hunks.baseline: No—he wanted to drink and laugh and talk with every Hunter who survived.
hunks.sol: No. He wanted to get drunk, laugh, and talk with every Hunter who survived.

hunks.baseline: And there was no doubt that…….
hunks.sol: And Jin would surely be there.

hunks.baseline: His voice, unable to reach anyone, was swallowed by the resonance and faded away.
hunks.sol: His unheard words dissolved into the reverberation.

hunks.baseline: Beyond the dazzling light that now filled the National Assembly, a young man’s figure flickered faintly across Magic Johnson’s vision.
hunks.sol: Through the blinding light now filling the National Assembly, Johnson caught a hazy glimpse of a young man.

hunks.baseline: And there was someone else running without hesitation toward him, toward the heart of the disaster.
hunks.sol: He saw someone else running toward him without hesitation—toward the heart of the disaster.

hunks.baseline: Something white as snow swept in like a wave.
hunks.sol: Something white as snow surged forward like a wave.

hunks.baseline: The moment it finished forming, sealing off every gap around the two beings standing at an impassable crossroads—Jin Taekyung and Michael Silbert—Magic Johnson gave a faint smile and awakened the mana throughout his body.
hunks.sol: It sealed every gap around Jin Taekyung and Michael Silbert, the two figures who stood opposed with neither able to give way.

preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: Then he spread it across the entire National Assembly, as if to envelop the whole world, and spoke.
hunks.sol: As it took shape, Magic Johnson smiled faintly and roused every bit of mana in his body. He spread it throughout the National Assembly as if to wrap the whole world in it, then spoke.

hunks.baseline: The spell, completed by devouring the Grand Mage’s vast reserves of mana, covered a radius of several hundred meters.
hunks.sol: The spell consumed the Grand Mage’s vast reserves of mana and spread across a radius of several hundred meters.

hunks.baseline: At last, a blinding flash burst forth, filling everyone’s vision.
hunks.sol: Then the light finally burst forth, filling everyone’s vision.

hunks.baseline: In the sliver of time between moments, split thinner and thinner—
hunks.sol: In a sliver of time divided into moments finer still—

hunks.baseline: *Bam! Rumble-rumble-rumble!*
hunks.sol: *Boom! Rumble-rumble-rumble!*

hunks.baseline: The world shook with a roar so immense it hurt. Pitch-black darkness and flashes of light flickered before my eyes over and over, while countless sensations coursed through my body.
hunks.sol: The world shook with a roar so vast it hurt. Pitch-black darkness and flashes of light flickered before my eyes. Sensations flooded through my body.

hunks.baseline: It hurt. It was hot. It was cold. It was wet.
hunks.sol: Pain. Heat. Cold. Wetness.

hunks.baseline: And…… it was heavy.
hunks.sol: And… weight.

hunks.baseline: So heavy that I could barely bear the weight crushing down on me even now.
hunks.sol: It pressed down on my whole body, almost more than I could bear.

hunks.baseline: My breathing was ragged. I struggled to clear my blurred vision, then drove the shaft of my spear into the ground to support myself.
hunks.sol: I struggled to clear my blurred vision, drove the shaft of my spear into the ground, and leaned on it.

hunks.baseline: In moments like this, I was glad I’d chosen a spear as my weapon.
hunks.sol: At times like this, I was glad I’d chosen a spear.

hunks.baseline: It reminded me of what the Instructor in the red cap had said when I first entered the Hunter Training Center, handing out weapons from the armory.
hunks.sol: It reminded me of what the red-capped Instructor had said when I first arrived at the Hunter Training Center and he handed out our weapons.

hunks.baseline: *“Yes. Sorry, but may I ask why?”*
hunks.sol: *“Yes, sir. Sorry, but may I ask why?”*

hunks.baseline: *“F-rank.”*
hunks.sol: *“F-rank, sir.”*

hunks.baseline: *“Right. There’s your answer. In a fight between weaklings like you, reach is everything. I know because I’ve used one myself. Another important thing is……”*
hunks.sol: *“Right. There’s your answer. In a fight between weaklings like you, reach is everything. I’ve used one, so I know. And another important thing…”*

hunks.baseline: *“What’s important?”*
hunks.sol: *“What’s that, sir?”*

hunks.baseline: *“Sorry, I didn’t quite catch that……?”*
hunks.sol: *“Sorry, I didn’t quite catch that…?”*

hunks.baseline: *“I said it looks cool. Now, listen. Say you run into an enemy. You fight like hell, one-on-one. You both pour out all your strength until you can’t even move a finger. In that situation, who’s going to fall over—the guy with the sword or the guy with the spear?”*
hunks.sol: *“I said it looks cool. Look. Say you meet an enemy. You fight like hell, one-on-one. You both use every last bit of strength until neither of you can lift a finger. Who falls over first—the guy with the sword or the guy with the spear?”*

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: *“I’d guess the one with weak legs.”*
hunks.sol: *“The guy with weaker legs, I’d think.”*

hunks.baseline: *“Wrong. The guy with the sword falls over first. Guaranteed.”*
hunks.sol: *“Wrong. The guy with the sword. Every time.”*

hunks.baseline: *“Could you perhaps explain why……?”*
hunks.sol: *“Could you tell me why, sir…?”*

hunks.baseline: I still couldn’t forget what the Instructor had said then, with a solemn expression.
hunks.sol: I still remembered the Instructor’s answer, delivered with a solemn expression.

hunks.baseline: *“Excuse me?”*

*“You jam it into the ground or a wall, and it’ll hold you up. But the guy with the sword is bound to fall over. Why? It’s short. That’s where the fight’s decided. One guy’s down, the other’s still standing. What do you think? Sounds like a scene from a movie, doesn’t it?”*
hunks.sol: *“Jam it into the ground or a wall and you’ve got something to lean on. The guy with the sword has to fall. Why? His sword’s too short. That’s what decides it: one man down, one man standing. What do you think? Like a scene from a movie, right?”*

hunks.baseline: *“Good. So, have you decided what weapon you’re going to use?”*
hunks.sol: *“Good. Decided what weapon you want?”*

hunks.baseline: *“Yes, I have.”*
hunks.sol: *“Yes, sir.”*

hunks.baseline: It was a stupid, dusty old memory.
hunks.sol: A stupid memory, and one I hadn’t thought of in years.

hunks.baseline: I’d gotten about twenty whacks on the ass with a spear shaft from the armory, then been practically forced to accept that spear as my first weapon.
hunks.sol: He’d promptly whacked me on the ass about twenty times with a spear shaft from the armory, then practically forced me to take that spear as my first weapon.

hunks.baseline: And when I saw that Instructor show up to our first training session the next day with a sword at his side, I learned one of the truths of the world.
hunks.sol: The next day, he turned up for our first training session with a sword at his side. I learned one of life’s great truths.

hunks.baseline: This line of work was crawling with some truly incredible assholes.
hunks.sol: This line of work was crawling with some truly spectacular assholes.

hunks.baseline: But even that Instructor, who must’ve stuck around the training center for the fun of messing with recruits like me, couldn’t have guessed back then.
hunks.sol: But even that Instructor, who must have stayed at the training center for the pleasure of messing with recruits like me, couldn’t have imagined where his stupid joke would lead.

hunks.baseline: That because of his stupid little joke, I’d be standing here now.
hunks.sol: That it would help keep me standing here.

hunks.baseline: That the F-rank Hunter he’d seen back then would make Michael Silbert kneel just a little over ten years later.
hunks.sol: That the F-rank Hunter he’d met would bring Michael Silbert to his knees a little over ten years later.

hunks.baseline: I raised my head at the heavy sound that pierced my ears.
hunks.sol: I lifted my head at the heavy sound.

hunks.baseline: Through my blurry vision, I saw a man trembling on one knee.
hunks.sol: Through my blurred vision, I saw him trembling on one knee.

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert, whose magical-power wings and gleaming black scales had both disappeared, stared at me, panting.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert’s wings of magical power were gone. So were his gleaming black scales. He stared at me, panting.

hunks.baseline: “Y-you bastard…….”
hunks.sol: “Y-you bastard…”

hunks.baseline: With a cough, a torrent of bloody fluid mixed with bits of his organs poured out.
hunks.sol: Blood and pieces of his organs poured from his mouth.

hunks.baseline: His body had spent all its magical power, and, despite his hopes, it showed none of the miraculous recovery it had displayed before.
hunks.sol: He’d exhausted all his magical power, and his body refused to heal as it had before, no matter how badly he wanted it to.

hunks.baseline: No. It would never do that again.
hunks.sol: No. It would never heal like that again.

hunks.baseline: He—Michael Silbert—was going to……
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert was going to…

hunks.baseline: I didn’t have the strength to say it out loud. I muttered the words where no one could hear them, gritted my teeth, and used White Flame to straighten up.
hunks.sol: I had no strength to say it aloud. I spoke the words in my head, gritted my teeth, and used White Flame to push myself upright.

hunks.baseline: *Thud.*
hunks.sol: *Step.*

hunks.baseline: Every step sent pain crashing through my body, as if I were about to break apart.
hunks.sol: Pain tore through my body with every step, as though I might break apart.

hunks.baseline: It was strange.
hunks.sol: Strange.

hunks.baseline: My eardrums had burst, and my ears had been ringing for a while, but the System’s warning beeps were still loud and annoying.
hunks.sol: My eardrums had burst, and my ears had been muffled for some time. Yet the System’s warnings still sounded loud and clear.

hunks.baseline: *Looks like my body’s pretty thoroughly wrecked.*
hunks.sol: *My body must be pretty thoroughly wrecked.*

hunks.baseline: I let out a hollow laugh, but it didn’t matter.
hunks.sol: A hollow laugh escaped me. It didn’t matter.

hunks.baseline: Since when had I worried about my condition before a fight?
hunks.sol: Since when had I ever worried about my condition in a fight?

hunks.baseline: I was happier that I’d finally brought Michael Silbert down—and that, despite the immense aftermath, all those familiar faces had made it through alive.
hunks.sol: What mattered was that I’d brought Michael Silbert down. And despite the force of that blast, the familiar faces around me were still alive.

hunks.baseline: Of course, not everyone felt the same joy I did.
hunks.sol: Not everyone shared my relief, of course.

hunks.baseline: “Jin Taekyung!”
hunks.sol: “Jin Taekyuuung!”

hunks.baseline: That middle-aged giant charging at me now, the Kronos Guild Master, was one of them.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged giant charging at me—the Kronos Guild Master—certainly didn’t.

hunks.baseline: As proof of how fierce the fighting had been, he’d lost an arm to some powerful fighter I couldn’t identify. Unable to accept that his life was over, he charged at me.
hunks.sol: He’d lost an arm to some powerful fighter in the battle. Unable to accept that his life was over, he came straight for me.

hunks.baseline: But the fierce whoosh that came from behind me forced him to accept it after all.
hunks.sol: Then a fierce rush of air sounded behind me, and he had no choice but to accept it.

hunks.baseline: An absurdly huge War Hammer swept past, and the Kronos Guild Master’s face disappeared.
hunks.sol: An absurdly huge War Hammer swept past. The Kronos Guild Master’s face vanished.

hunks.baseline: Behind his corpse, which crumpled like a rotten log, Chuck Hagel stood posed like a shot-putter.
hunks.sol: Behind his body, which crumpled like a rotten log, Chuck Hagel stood in the pose of a shot-putter.

hunks.baseline: After staring intently at me for a brief moment, he let out a short laugh and turned away. Then he charged the remaining traitors.
hunks.sol: He stared at me for a moment, let out a short laugh, and turned to charge the remaining traitors.

hunks.baseline: With a warm little line to thaw their frozen hearts.
hunks.sol: He had a warm little line to thaw their frozen hearts.

hunks.baseline: “Let’s see you keep playing to the very end, you sons of bitches.”
hunks.sol: “Let’s keep playing to the end, you sons of bitches.”

hunks.baseline: Cheers and screams mingled in my ringing ears. Some fell, spraying blood; others stepped over their bodies and pressed on.
hunks.sol: Cheers and screams mingled in my muffled ears. Some fell, spraying blood. Others stepped over their bodies and pressed on.

hunks.baseline: The tide had already turned.
hunks.sol: The tide had turned.

hunks.baseline: Even if the goddess of fate showed up to tip the scales back, all we had to do was take her down, too.
hunks.sol: Even if the goddess of fate came down to tip the scales back, we could take her down too.

hunks.baseline: Like the monster struggling to rise as I came within a few steps of him.
hunks.sol: Just as I would take down the monster struggling to rise now that I was right in front of him.

hunks.baseline: *Thud.*
hunks.sol: *Step.*

hunks.baseline: I suddenly stopped. And, like an old man leaning on his cane after a long journey to visit a lifelong friend, I greeted him, weary but glad to see him.
hunks.sol: I stopped. Like an old man who had leaned on his cane through a long journey to see a lifelong friend, I greeted him, weary but glad to have arrived.

hunks.baseline: In reply, all I got was the still-brilliant blue gleam of his sword.
hunks.sol: His answer was the still-brilliant blue blade of his sword.

hunks.baseline: But even the sharp edge forged from Dragon Bone—a material without peer—couldn’t cut through Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron. And the strength and speed behind the sword were nowhere near enough.
hunks.sol: But even an edge forged from Dragon Bone, a material beyond compare, couldn’t cut through Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron. There was nowhere near enough strength or speed behind the strike.

hunks.baseline: Not enough to get past even me, a man who was practically a hospital patient.
hunks.sol: Even I, barely able to stand, could block it with ease.

hunks.baseline: Not enough to stop me from returning that rude answer.
hunks.sol: And return his rude greeting.

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert’s eyes flew wide open. His arms crumpled, the pain so intense that a scream, mixed with blood, bubbled up from his gaping mouth before he could even let it out.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert’s eyes flew wide. Both arms crumpled. Blood and a scream he couldn’t force out bubbled in his open mouth.

hunks.baseline: Blood spurted intermittently, splattering my face.
hunks.sol: Blood spurted across my face.

hunks.baseline: But why?
hunks.sol: Why, then, did it smell so foul?

hunks.baseline: If I thought about what he’d done up until now, the scent of blood seeping into my nose should have been sweet. But all I could smell was something revolting.
hunks.sol: After everything he’d done, I would have thought the scent of his blood would be sweet. Instead, it sickened me.

hunks.baseline: Maybe that was why I suddenly stopped.
hunks.sol: Maybe that was why I stopped.

hunks.baseline: Why my own face, reflected in those eyes darkened by blood and tears, looked twisted like a monster’s.
hunks.sol: Why the face reflected in his eyes, dark with blood and tears, looked twisted into a monster’s.

hunks.baseline: “……So this is the world you wanted so badly?”
hunks.sol: “…So this is the world you wanted so badly?”

hunks.baseline: I knew.
No matter what I asked, he wouldn’t give me the answer I wanted.
hunks.sol: I knew he couldn’t give me the answer I wanted, no matter what I asked.

hunks.baseline: No answer could calm this heart and these emotions threatening to burst out of me.
hunks.sol: No answer could settle the feelings threatening to burst out of me.

hunks.baseline: But…… I still wanted to hear it. I had to hear it.
hunks.sol: But I still wanted to hear him speak. I had to.

hunks.baseline: For the countless people who had died because of the pathetic ambition he’d held on to.
hunks.sol: For all the people who had died because of his pathetic ambition.

hunks.baseline: *Grab.*
I seized Michael Silbert by his one remaining horn and hauled him upright. Enduring the pain flooding over me, I whispered to him as he died by the second.
hunks.sol: I seized Michael Silbert’s one remaining horn and hauled him upright. Fighting the pain that surged through me, I whispered to him as he slipped closer to death.

hunks.baseline: And in the next moment—
hunks.sol: And then I understood.

hunks.baseline: I realized where his other horn had gone. Why it was nowhere to be seen.
hunks.sol: I knew where his other horn had gone. Why I hadn’t seen it anywhere nearby.

hunks.baseline: *Thump.*
hunks.sol: *Thud.*

hunks.baseline: With a dull, wet sound, the horn shot up from somewhere and pierced someone’s palm.
hunks.sol: The horn shot up from somewhere and pierced a palm with a dull, wet sound.

hunks.baseline: But there was no blood, though blood should have poured out. No groan of pain held back.
hunks.sol: But there was no blood. No groan from someone enduring the pain.

hunks.baseline: All that filled the empty space was Michael Silbert’s trembling eyes, fixed over my shoulder, and his voice.
hunks.sol: Only Michael Silbert’s trembling gaze, fixed over my shoulder, and his voice.

hunks.baseline: “How dare you… How dare a monster like you…….”
hunks.sol: “How dare… How dare a monster like you…”

hunks.baseline: “Wrong. I’ll tell you this once, and only once, so you’d better remember it.”
hunks.sol: “Wrong. I’ll tell you once, and only once, so remember it.”

hunks.baseline: At that familiar voice reaching my ears, I realized who was standing behind me and laughed out loud.
hunks.sol: I knew that voice. I realized who stood behind me and laughed aloud.
